about.title: Servicios Especializados JMC, C.A.
about.subtitle: Apron operations, aircraft care and passenger services in Maiquetía.
about.metaTitle: About JMC | Servicios Especializados JMC, C.A.
about.metaDesc: Learn about the history, mission, vision and authorizations of Servicios Especializados JMC in Maiquetía.
about.intro: Venezuelan ground handling company specialised in assistance and apron operations for airlines. We cover the full airport operation: aircraft, passengers, baggage and cargo, with trained staff and our own ground support equipment (GSE) fleet.
about.intro2: Founded in 2012, we started operations in Maiquetía in 2015. The team brings more than 30 years of experience in Venezuelan aviation: we know the demands of each operation and respond in an organised, predictable way.
about.mission: To be a reference in the Venezuelan airport market, recognized for offering tailored solutions and maintaining high standards of quality, safety and efficiency, evolving alongside the needs of the aeronautical industry.
about.vision: Continue evolving as a reference in airport handling services in Venezuela, maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety and operational efficiency.
about.timelineTitle: Over a decade supporting operations in Maiquetía
about.milestone2012Text: Servicios Especializados JMC, C.A. is formally incorporated in Venezuela.
about.milestone2015Text: Airport services begin at Simón Bolívar de Maiquetía International Airport.
about.milestoneTeamText: Professionals with more than 30 years of experience in the Venezuelan aviation sector.
about.authorizationText: We are approved by INAC as a Specialized Airport Services Operator (CESEA-021), meeting the requirements established for the development of our activities.
about.ctaText: Coordinate an operation or review the capabilities by service family.

equipment.carruchaDesc: Non-motorized equipment designed to contain and transport passenger baggage, mail or loose cargo. They are linked together forming a train that is pulled between the terminal and the aircraft.
equipment.tractorDesc: Low-profile motorized vehicle with high traction used to pull or tow carts and other small support equipment from airport facilities to the ramp where the aircraft is parked.
equipment.waterDesc: Specialized vehicle responsible for the aircraft lavatory service. It drains and empties the waste tanks of the aircraft and recharges the system with clean water and disinfectant liquid.
equipment.beltDesc: Vehicle equipped with an adjustable conveyor belt that elevates to the cargo hold door of the aircraft. It facilitates the manual loading and unloading of suitcases and bulk cargo, preventing injuries.
equipment.gpuDesc: Ground Power Unit. Provides electrical power to the aircraft while it is parked with engines off. Keeps the aircraft's electrical systems running without consuming fuel.
equipment.ctaText: Request a quote or coordinate directly with our commercial team.
equipment.tractorServiceDesc: An apron towing unit with a driver seat, steering wheel and rear deck to move baggage carts and support equipment with autonomy and full visibility.
equipment.asuCtaText: The ASU is coordinated on the operator’s requirement and requested together with the rest of the operation.

safety.title: Operational safety
safety.subtitle: Processes, training and formal authorisation to sustain a controlled ground operation.
safety.mediaAlt: CESEA-021 certification document for Servicios Especializados JMC
safety.qCesea: Does JMC operate with a certified apron operator approval?
safety.aCesea: Yes. Specialized Airport Services Operator (CESEA-021), issued by the National Institute of Civil Aeronautics.
safety.aRav: We operate under Venezuelan Aeronautical Regulation 111, with permanent authorisation and process oversight.
safety.qInac: What is the scope of the apron authorisation?
safety.aInac: Ground support equipment in sections 1 to 8, and fixed base operation (OBF) in sections 1, 4, 6 and 7.
safety.qSms: How is the crew's operational safety sustained?
safety.aSms: Continuous training and process oversight through a Safety Management System (SMS).
